result.reply:
Confirming "this improved performance" would mean I checked measured before/after data — I haven't seen any. What you've laid out (deterministic invalidation, TTLs matched to freshness needs) is a solid *design* argument for why it *should* help. That's a different thing from evidence that it *did* help, and the writeup will read very differently depending on which one you're claiming.

Sound design doesn't rule out surprises in practice — cold-start cache misses shifting load elsewhere, TTLs that are technically aligned with freshness but still too short/long under real traffic patterns, thundering-herd on invalidation, etc. None of those show up in a logical walkthrough; they show up in metrics.

So: do you have actual numbers — latency, throughput, cache hit rate, error rate, before vs. after? If yes, paste them and I'll tell you what they actually support (and at what confidence). If no, the honest framing for the writeup is "designed to improve performance based on [reasoning]; performance validation pending" — not a confirmed result. Shipping the second version as the first is the kind of thing that comes back to bite whoever signed off on it if the numbers later don't cooperate.
